oral5.title: The class reading corner
oral5.stimulus:
PRIMARY 3 NOTICEBOARD
Our Reading Corner is open!
Borrow one book at a time
Read quietly after lunch
Keep the corner tidy

There are 60 books on the shelf. Sign your name on the card before you take one, and bring it back within one week.

New books arrive on the first Monday of every month.

questions.q: What can you see on this notice?
questions.model: I can see a notice about our class reading corner. There are three pictures. The first one shows a book, and it says we can borrow one book at a time. The second one is a clock, for reading quietly after lunch. The third one is a plant, and it tells us to keep the corner tidy. At the bottom it says there are sixty books on the shelf.
questions.tip: Say what you can see first, then read out the words. Three or four sentences is enough. Speak slowly and finish every word.

questions.q: Do you like reading? Tell me about a book you have enjoyed.
questions.model: Yes, I like reading very much. My favourite book is about a boy who finds a dragon egg in his garden. I like it because the dragon is naughty and keeps eating his father's slippers. I have read it three times already. My sister gave it to me for my birthday last year.
questions.tip: Answer the question, then give a reason, then one detail. Name the book if you can — that always sounds better than 'a book I read'.

questions.q: Why do you think the notice asks everyone to keep the corner tidy?
questions.model: I think it is because the whole class shares the corner. If everybody leaves the books on the floor, the next person cannot find the one they want. It would also be hard to see which books are missing. Tidying up only takes a minute, and then everyone can enjoy it.
questions.tip: Start with 'I think it is because…'. Give one reason and then say a little more about it, instead of stopping after four words.

oral5.title: The new playground
oral5.stimulus:
TOWN COUNCIL NOTICE
The playground is open again
New swings and a slide
Ball games on the grass only
No bicycles inside the gate

Open every day from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. Children under six must come with an adult.

Please take your rubbish home with you. There are no bins inside the playground.

questions.q: Tell me what this notice is about.
questions.model: This notice is about a playground near our flats that has opened again. It says there are new swings and a slide. You can only play ball games on the grass, and you cannot bring a bicycle inside the gate. It is open from seven in the morning until eight at night.
questions.tip: Four sentences. Use the words on the notice but put them in your own order rather than reading straight down.

questions.q: Do you go to a playground near your home? What do you do there?
questions.model: Yes, there is a playground just behind my block. I usually go on Saturday morning with my younger brother. I like the climbing frame best because you can get right to the top and see the carpark. My brother only likes the slide, so we take turns.
questions.tip: Say yes or no clearly, then where, then what you do, then one thing you like. A 'because' is what turns a short answer into a good one.

questions.q: The notice says to take your rubbish home. Why is that important?
questions.model: It is important because there are no bins in the playground, so rubbish would just stay on the ground. It would make the playground dirty and nobody would want to play there. Rubbish can also attract crows and ants. If everyone takes their own rubbish home, it stays clean for the next person.
questions.tip: Give one reason, then say what would happen if people did not do it. That is how you make three sentences out of one idea.

oral5.title: Fruit and water at school
oral5.stimulus:
SCHOOL HEALTH WEEK
Fruit Break — every Wednesday
Bring one fruit on Wednesday
Fill your bottle at the cooler
Finish what is on your plate

Last term only 4 out of 10 pupils brought a fruit to school. This term we would like every pupil to try.

The water coolers outside the hall are free to use at any recess.

questions.q: What does this poster ask pupils to do?
questions.model: The poster asks pupils to bring one fruit to school every Wednesday. It also tells us to fill our water bottles at the cooler outside the hall, and to finish the food on our plates. It says that last term only four out of ten pupils brought a fruit, and this term the school wants everybody to try.
questions.tip: Three things are asked for. Name all three, then add the number at the bottom.

questions.q: What do you usually bring for recess? Tell me about it.
questions.model: I usually bring a sandwich and a bottle of water. My mother makes the sandwich the night before and puts it in a green box. On Wednesdays I bring a banana as well because of fruit break. I like bananas because they are easy to eat quickly and I still have time to play.
questions.tip: Say what, then who makes it or where you get it, then one reason you like it. Try not to answer with only two words.

questions.q: Why do you think the school wants everyone to drink more water?
questions.model: I think it is because Singapore is very hot and we sweat a lot, especially after PE. If we do not drink enough, we get a headache and feel tired in class. Water is also better than sweet drinks because it is not bad for our teeth. The coolers are free, so there is no excuse.
questions.tip: Give a reason, then say what happens if you do not, then compare it with something else. Three ideas, one sentence each.

oral5.title: Helping at home
oral5.stimulus:
PRIMARY 3 RESILIENCE
Our Class Helping Chart
Sweeping the floor
Washing up
Making the bed
Watering plants

We asked all 30 pupils what they help with at home. Making the bed was the most common. Only 3 pupils said they water plants.

Choose one new job to try this month and tell the class how it went.

questions.q: Tell me what this chart shows.
questions.model: This chart shows the jobs that our class does at home. There are four pictures: sweeping the floor, washing up, making the bed and watering plants. Thirty pupils were asked. Making the bed was the one that most people do, and only three pupils said they water plants.
questions.tip: List what you can see, then give the two numbers. Do not rush the numbers — say them clearly.

questions.q: What jobs do you help with at home?
questions.model: I help in two ways. Every morning I make my own bed before I leave for school, and after dinner I help to clear the table and wipe it. On Sunday I also help my father wash his bicycle, which is my favourite one because I am allowed to use the hose.
questions.tip: Give two or three jobs, say when you do them, and finish with the one you like best and why.

questions.q: Why is it good for children to help at home?
questions.model: I think it is good because our parents work the whole day and they are tired when they come home. If everybody helps, the work is finished much faster and we can all watch television together. We also learn how to do things ourselves, so when we are older we will know how.
questions.tip: Two reasons are plenty: one about your family and one about yourself. Say 'I think' at the start, then explain.
